text:
24-hour news summary.

1. 1 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5666) A digest highlighted Anthropic’s subscription value, Ghost AI’s Core computer, Cua’s natural cursor motions, Airbnb’s AI spending, and China’s growing strength in large language models.
2. 2 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5668) An English digest covered AI agents finding magnetic semiconductor candidates, Anthropic’s subscription value, Ghost AI’s Core, Cua Driver, Airbnb’s AI investment, and Chinese model progress.
3. 3 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5669) Dax argued that rapidly improving models are making many elaborate custom workflows obsolete, with vanilla Codex increasingly delivering state-of-the-art results.
4. 4 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5671) Tibo argues that agents will soon handle most internet actions, model pickers will disappear, models will become dramatically better and cheaper, plugins may become a major ecosystem, and taste will matter more than typing speed.
5. 5 Mistral introduced Large 4, a natively multimodal one-trillion-parameter model with 49 billion active parameters, API access today, and an open-weights release planned for October.
6. 6 Meta open-sourced Rebalancer, an assignment solver handling about 40 million infrastructure allocation problems daily with both exact and parallel local-search methods.
7. 7 Vals AI reported that more than 90 Claude agents identified two candidate magnetic semiconductors, including one material synthesized in 1999, in three days of simulations.
8. 8 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5675) Mustafa Suleyman shared an article without additional commentary.
9. 9 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5676) A study found that two different coding agents reviewing each other’s patches caught more silent bugs than giving one agent a larger budget, raising fully correct patches from 45.8% to 62.5%.
10. 10 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5677) Google introduced open multimodal EmbeddingGemma 2, a lightweight 740-million-parameter model for text, code, image, video, and audio embeddings, available on Hugging Face.
11. 11 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5678) Google introduced Nano Banana 2.1, an upgraded image-generation and editing model with improvements in visual design, masking, and subject consistency.
12. 12 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5680) Cortex introduced a robot-control platform combining language-directed actions, remote human guidance, and models including GPT-6 Astra, Claude, Gemini, and open-weight systems.
13. 13 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5681) Anthropic expanded its Claude Startups program with a year of Claude Team, API credits, tool discounts, and access to applied-AI office hours.
14. 14 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5682) Sonia Baschez called for an AI assistant that proactively manages family logistics, errands, appointments, bills, shopping, and other mental-load responsibilities.
15. 15 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5683) Oki Home announced a personal AI computer designed to keep consumer data under users’ control, with first-batch reservations shipping in mid-December.
16. 16 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5684) Anthropic expanded its Cyber Verification Program, giving verified security professionals access to advanced Claude models for defensive work and authorized offensive testing.
17. 17 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5685) Claude can now work directly inside Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides, reading and editing files in a sidebar with user approval.
18. 18 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5686) Minerva Humanoids emerged from stealth with $10 million in funding to build semi-autonomous humanoids for hazardous energy, explosives, and materials-response jobs.
19. 19 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5687) OpenAI reportedly planned to release hundreds of newly solved mathematical problems, prompting researchers to publish related work ahead of the announcement.
20. 20 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5688) AgentMail introduced AgentID, a “Sign in with Google” style authentication system for AI agents. (1/2)
